issue_context.title: Bug in `rolling` method on Expr, it's failing to keep track of its dependent expressions properly
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```
>>> pl.col("a").rolling("hi", period="10ms").meta.root_names()
['a']
>>> pl.col("a").rolling("hi", period="10ms")
<Expr ['col("a").over([])'] at 0x7FA44A42B8D0>
```

Notice that the expr doesn't keep track of a dependence on "hi", thus if you use this expr in a `select`, the `collect` will fail. You'll won't notice this will fail until collect time.


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

It should keep track of the dependence on "hi"

### Expected behavior

```
>>> pl.col("a").rolling("hi", period="10ms").meta.root_names()
['a', 'hi']
>>> pl.col("a").rolling("hi", period="10ms")
<Expr ['col("a").over("["hi"])'] at 0x7FA44A42B8D0>
```

### Installed versions

<details>

```
--------Version info---------

Index type:           UInt32
Platform:             Linux-6.2.6-76060206-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
```

comments:
`rolling` is actually a little bit special as its `index_column` doesn't exist in the form of an `expression`...

In any case, this query shouldn't raise. Unfortunately, during the optimization, this index column was pruned unexpected.
